title: Bench Diary Rule for Counting the Days a Change Gives Back
content:
# Bench Diary Rule for Counting the Days a Change Gives Back

Three dates can start the count of the bench days a change gives back on a commission under Belrose Design Studio Custom Commissions: the date the stone setting stage was reached, the date the casting stage was reached and the date production began. Which of them starts it turns on the stages of production standing recorded on the commission.

## The rule

1. Where a stone setting stage stands recorded on the commission and no final inspection stage stands recorded on it, the bench days the change gives back are counted from the date the stone setting stage was reached.
2. Where a casting stage stands recorded on the commission and no stone setting stage stands recorded on it, they are counted from the date the casting stage was reached.
3. Otherwise they are counted from the date production began.

In every case the days run to the day the change is priced and are never fewer than none.

## The stages the rule reads

The dates the casting stage, the stone setting stage and the final inspection stage were reached stand on the commission's own production stage entries; a stage stands recorded where an entry for it has been booked, and stands unrecorded where none has.

## Dated readings (hypothetical)

A commission on which production began on the 1st of March, the casting stage was reached on the 10th of March and the stone setting stage on the 20th of March, with the change priced on the 30th of March.

| What stands recorded | Counted from | Days |
|---|---|---|
| Casting and stone setting recorded, no final inspection | The 20th of March | 10 |
| Casting recorded, no stone setting | The 10th of March | 20 |
| Casting, stone setting and final inspection all recorded | The 1st of March | 29 |
| No stage recorded at all | The 1st of March | 29 |
